lessons.title: Variables, types, and f-strings
lessons.focus: Names, objects, f-strings, tuples, and formatting.
lessons.hint: Start with an f-string. For a type name, ask the object for its type's __name__.

lessons.title: Numbers, division, and operators
lessons.focus: Floor division, modulo, averages, and compound interest.
lessons.goal: Use Python's number operators with confidence.
lessons.hint: The four tools are //, %, sum()/len(), and **. Guard the empty list before dividing.

lessons.title: Strings and slicing
lessons.focus: Slices, immutable strings, joins, and whitespace.
lessons.goal: Transform text with Python's expressive string tools.
lessons.hint: Reverse with [::-1]. Use split() with no argument for words and join() for pieces.

lessons.title: Conditionals and truthiness
lessons.focus: If statements, truthy values, early returns, and grades.
lessons.goal: Teach your program to choose the right path.
lessons.hint: Check the highest grade first. A blank string becomes empty after strip(), and empty is falsy.

lessons.title: Loops and iteration
lessons.focus: for, while, range, enumerate, and repeated computation.
lessons.goal: Use loops to process sequences and repeat work reliably.
lessons.hint: Remember that range stops before its end. Check FizzBuzz's divisible-by-15 case before 3 or 5.

lessons.title: Functions and arguments
lessons.focus: Defaults, *args, **kwargs, callbacks, and safe mutable arguments.
lessons.goal: Build reusable functions with flexible, predictable inputs.
lessons.hint: Use None as the default for a list you create inside the function; *args is a tuple and **kwargs is a dict.

lessons.title: Lists and methods
lessons.focus: append, extend, slicing, deduplication, rotation, and chunks.
lessons.goal: Transform lists while keeping order, copies, and boundaries clear.
lessons.hint: append adds one item while extend adds each item. Guard an empty list before using n % len(items).

lessons.title: Tuples and unpacking
lessons.focus: Immutable records, multiple returns, starred unpacking, and coordinates.
lessons.goal: Use tuples to represent fixed-size data and unpack it cleanly.
lessons.hint: Write first, *rest = items for a head and the remaining list. Raise ValueError when there is no minimum or maximum.

lessons.title: Dictionaries
lessons.focus: Key-value lookup, get, setdefault, merging, and grouping.
lessons.goal: Model and transform related data with Python's key-value workhorse.
lessons.hint: Use get(key, 0) for counts and setdefault(letter, []) when a group must stay stored in the dictionary.

lessons.title: Sets
lessons.focus: Uniqueness, membership, intersections, differences, and set algebra.
lessons.goal: Use sets for fast membership and clear operations on collections.
lessons.hint: Build sets with set(iterable), use & for items in both and - for items only in the first, then sort list results.

lessons.title: Comprehensions
lessons.focus: List, set, dict, nested, and generator comprehensions.
lessons.goal: Build collections clearly with compact, readable comprehensions.
lessons.hint: Read a comprehension left to right: expression, for each item, where the optional if filters; nested for clauses follow normal loop order.

lessons.title: Sorting with keys
lessons.focus: Key functions, tuple keys, stable sorting, versions, and max.
lessons.goal: Sort data by multiple rules without writing comparators.
lessons.hint: Use tuple keys for tie-breakers, negate numeric fields for descending counts, and split version parts into integers before sorting.

lessons.title: Scope and closures
lessons.focus: LEGB lookup, nonlocal state, factories, and late binding.
lessons.goal: Create functions that retain private state after their factory returns.
lessons.hint: Reading an enclosing name is free; use nonlocal when rebinding it, and bind loop values with a default argument to avoid late binding.

lessons.title: First-class functions
lessons.focus: Passing, returning, composing, and applying functions and lambdas.
lessons.goal: Use functions as flexible building blocks for reusable pipelines.
lessons.hint: Pass func without parentheses, compose right-to-left, pipeline left-to-right, and make an empty pipeline return its input unchanged.

lessons.title: Decorators
lessons.focus: Wrappers, forwarding arguments, function attributes, and memoization.
lessons.goal: Extend functions with reusable behavior while preserving their call shape.
lessons.hint: A decorator takes a function and returns a closure; forward with *args and **kwargs, and keep caches in the enclosing scope.

lessons.title: Decorators with arguments
lessons.focus: Decorator factories, retries, repeats, and functools.wraps.
lessons.goal: Build configurable decorators that preserve names and docstrings.
lessons.hint: Use three nested layers—arguments, function, then call—and apply functools.wraps(func) to the innermost wrapper.

lessons.title: The functools toolkit
lessons.focus: reduce, partial, lru_cache, operator functions, and nested lookup.
lessons.goal: Use focused functional tools to express folds, reusable calls, and fast recursion.
lessons.hint: Choose identity values for reduce, prefill with partial, decorate Fibonacci with lru_cache, and reduce getitem over a key path.

lessons.title: Type hints
lessons.focus: Modern annotations, unions, generic sequences, and type introspection.
lessons.goal: Annotate functions precisely so tools and readers understand their contracts.
lessons.hint: Use list[str], int | None, and Sequence[T]; annotate the widest accepted input and remember hints document rather than enforce.
